titleStmt.author: Dehaene
Changeux

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Experimental and Theoretical Approaches to Conscious Processing

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: We confront these findings to current theoretical models of conscious processing, including the Global Neuronal Workspace (GNW) model according to which conscious access occurs when incoming information is made globally available to multiple brain systems through a network of neurons with long-range axons densely distributed in prefrontal, parieto-temporal and cingulate cortices.

span.label: conscious access
span.quote: In this review, we outline recent advances made in understanding the delimited issue of conscious access: how does an external or internal piece of information gain access to conscious processing, defined as a reportable subjective experience?

span.label: review
span.quote: The present review focuses on the well-delimited issue of how an external or internal piece of information goes beyond non-conscious processing and gains access to conscious processing, a transition characterized by the existence of a reportable subjective experience.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: incoming activity that exceeds a dynamical threshold ignites a self-supporting reverberating cell assembly which sustains the conscious content and broadcasts it to distant sites
span.quote: Such a selfconnected system exhibits a dynamical threshold: if the incoming activity carries sufficient weight, it leads to the ignition of a self-supporting, reverberating, temporary, metastable, and distributed cell assembly that represents the current conscious contents and broadcasts it to virtually all distant sites.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: global broadcasting frees information from encapsulated circuits and makes it available to many processors, including the ones that formulate verbal reports, which is why conscious information is reportable
span.quote: Global broadcasting allows information to be more efficiently processed (because it it no longer confined to a subset of non-conscious circuits, but can be flexibly shared by many cortical processors) and to be verbally reported (because these processors include those involved in formulating verbal messages).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: during ignition the workspace is mobilised as a whole, with the non-selected neurons actively inhibited, which blocks a second simultaneous ignition and produces the serial bottleneck
span.quote: Such a disruption occurs because during ignition, the GNW is mobilized as a whole, some GNW neurons being active while the rest is actively inhibited, thus preventing multiple simultaneous ignitions.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: spontaneous prestimulus fluctuations barely affect the fast feedforward stage but strongly bias the slow NMDA-based reverberating stage, so an identical stimulus ignites on some trials and not others, producing all-or-none perception
span.quote: In GNW simulations, prestimulus fluctuations in neural discharges only have a small effect on the early sensory stage, which largely reflects objective stimulus amplitude and duration, but they have a large influence on the second slower stage, which is characterized by NMDA-based reverberating integration and ultimately leads to a bimodal "all-ornone" distribution of activity

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: a weak stimulus produces a feedforward wave that cannot recruit enough self-sustaining reverberation, so it dies out before the late global activation and stays subliminal
span.quote: For very brief or low-amplitude stimuli, a feedforward wave was seen in the initial thalamic and cortical stages of the simulation, but it died out without triggering the late global activation, because it was not able to gather sufficient selfsustaining reverberant activation (Dehaene and Changeux, 2005).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: because far more workspace neurons are laterally inhibited than activated, the summed scalp signal during ignition is net positive, which is why conscious access shows up as the positive P3b
span.quote: Thus, the model can explain why, during conscious access, the resulting event-related potential is dominated by a positive waveform, the P3b.

span.label: The review deliberately covers only conscious access, not higher-order concepts of consciousness
span.quote: The present review was deliberately limited to conscious access.

span.label: Higher-order concepts such as metacognition and self-representation are excluded because the authors judge them insufficiently defined empirically
span.quote: Thus, our view is that these concepts, although essential, have not yet received a sufficient empirical and neurophysiological definition to figure in this review.

span.label: The supporting simulations implement only a small fragment of the proposed architecture
span.quote: Although the full GNW architecture was not simulated, four areas were selected and hierarchically interconnected (figure 7).

span.label: Lesion and TMS evidence does not establish that prefrontal contribution is causally necessary for conscious perception
span.quote: While suggestive, these observations do not quite suffice to establish that a frontal contribution is causally necessary for conscious perception.

span.label: The field's strict operational criterion is stated to OVERESTIMATE the thing it measures: subjects perform above chance while denying they perceived anything.
span.quote: This strict objective criterion raises problems, however (Persaud et al., 2007; Schurger and Sher, 2008). First, it tends to overestimate conscious perception: there are many conditions in which subjects perform better than chance

span.label: Which task counts as evidence is unresolved, because performance can be at chance on one task and not another.
span.quote: Second, performance can be at chance level for some tasks, but not others, raising the issue of which tasks count as evidence of conscious perception or merely of subliminal processing.

span.label: The verdict rests on accepting a null hypothesis, and the review states the significance often depends on an analyst's choice of how many trials to run.
span.quote: Third, the approach requires accepting the null hypothesis of chance-level performance, yet performance never really falls down to zero, and whether it is significant or not often depends on arbitrary choices such as the number of trials dedicated to its measurement.

span.label: the concept of a stochastic phase transition, used to describe the sudden switch of the network into the ignited conscious state
span.quote: The transition to the ignited state can be described, in theoretical physics terms, as a stochastic phase transition – a sudden change in neuronal dynamics whose occurrence depends in part on stimulus characteristics and in part on spontaneous fluctuations in activity (Dehaene and Changeux, 2005; Dehaene et al., 2003b).

span.label: the blackboard architecture - a shared data structure updated by many specialised modules - taken over as the global workspace of consciousness
span.quote: However, capitalizing on the earlier concept of a blackboard 22 system in artificial intelligence (a common data structure shared and updated by many specialized modules), Baars (1989) proposed an homunculus-free psychological model where the current conscious content is represented within a distinct mental space called global workspace, with the capacity to broadcast this information to a set of other processors (figure 6).

span.label: conscious access - BY THE OBJECTIVE CRITERION: a stimulus counts as non-conscious only if subjects cannot perform above chance on a direct task, a tradition grounded in signal-detection theory
span.quote: According to a long psychophysical tradition, grounded in signal-detection theory, a stimulus should be accepted as non-conscious only if subjects are unable to perform above chance on some direct task of stimulus detection or classification.

span.label: conscious access - BY SUBJECTIVE CRITERIA: visibility ratings, or second-order commentaries such as post-decision wagering, adopted BECAUSE the objective criterion fails
span.quote: For these reasons, recent alternative approaches emphasize either pure subjective reports, such as ratings of stimulus visibility

span.label: attention - James's classic definition, which the review says CONFLATES two processes that are now clearly separable
span.quote: The problem with this definition is that it conflates two processes that are now clearly separa

span.label: builds-on → Crick and Koch (1990) programme on the neural correlates of consciousness
span.quote: Following Crick and Koch (Crick and Koch, 1990), we focussed solely here on the simpler and well-studied question of what neurophysiological mechanisms differentiate conscious access to some information from nonconscious processing of the same information.

span.label: builds-on → Dehaene et al. (1998a) global neuronal workspace architecture
span.quote: The main anatomical premise of the GNW model is that it consists of “a distributed set of cortical neurons characterized by their ability to receive from and send back to homologous neurons in other cortical areas horizontal projections through longrange excitatory axons mostly originating from the pyramidal cells of layers II and III” (Dehaene et al., 1998a) and more densely distributed in prefrontal and inferior parietal cortices.

span.label: conscious access —distinct-from→ attention
span.quote: Conscious access must be distinguished from the related concept of attention.

span.label: Granger causality
span.quote: (as assessed by Granger causality, a statistical technique that measures whether the time course of signals at one site can forecast the future evolution of signals at another distant site)

span.label: correlation (coefficient of determination)
span.quote: For instance, in visual masking, the conscious perception thresholds derived from objective and subjective data are essentially identical across subjects (r²=0.96, slope≈1) (Del Cul et al., 2006).

span.label: sensitivity and specificity
span.quote: In relation with the GNW model, it is noteworthy that prediction of non-recovery after 1 year could be calculated with up to 86% sensitivity and 97% specificity when taking into account both diffusion tensor and spectroscopic measures of cortical white matter integrity (Tshibanda et al., 2009).

span.label: independent component analysis
span.quote: Reduced activity in a "resting-state" distributed cortical network in three vegetative state patients, as measured by independent component analysis of fMRI data (Cauda et al., 2009).

span.label: Across many paradigms, conscious access is marked by three convergent physiological signatures: late amplification of the relevant sensory activity, long-distance cortico-cortical synchronisation in the beta and gamma bands, and ignition of a large-scale prefronto-parietal network.
span.quote: In conclusion, human neuroimaging methods and electrophysiological recordings during conscious access, under a broad variety of paradigms, consistently reveal a late amplification of relevant sensory activity, long-distance cortico-cortical synchronisation at beta and gamma frequencies, and "ignition" of a large-scale prefronto-parietal network.

span.label: Subliminal influence shrinks as processing depth increases, leaving only small effects at high-level cognitive and decision stages.
span.quote: First, subliminal priming quickly decreases with processing depth, such that only small influences are detectable at higher cognitive and decision levels (Dehaene, 2008; van Gaal et al., 2008).

span.label: Subliminal priming decays with time and is typically undetectable beyond about 500 ms.
span.quote: Second, subliminal priming decreases with elapsed time, and therefore typically ceases to be detectable after 500 ms (Dupoux et al., 2008; Greenwald et al., 1996; Mattler, 2005).

span.label: Subliminal stimuli do not produce durable or flexible changes in executive control.
span.quote: Third, subliminal stimuli typically fail to yield lasting and flexible modifications in executive control.

span.label: The first roughly 200 ms of visual processing is fully preserved on trials where the subject reports not seeing the stimulus, so early sensory activity does not distinguish conscious from non-conscious trials.
span.quote: Evidence from the attentional blink also confirms that the first 200 ms of initial visual processing can be fully preserved on trials in which subjects deny seeing a stimulus (Sergent et al., 2005; Vogel et al., 1998)

span.label: The most reliable electrophysiological correlate of visibility is the late, broadly distributed positive P3/P3b component at about 300-500 ms, distinct from the earlier focal anterior P3a which can occur non-consciously.
span.quote: In ERPs, the most consistent correlate of visibility appears to be a late (~300-500 ms) and broadly distributed positive component called P3 or sometimes P3b

span.label: In monkeys viewing binocular rivalry, the share of neurons whose firing follows the reported percept rises steeply from primary visual cortex to higher associative cortex, supporting the idea that conscious assemblies are denser in higher areas.
span.quote: The proportion of such cells increased from about 20% in V1/V2 to 40% in V4, MT or MST, to as high as 90% in IT and STS.

span.label: Conscious words modulated late activity at 68.8% of intracranial electrode sites versus 24.4% for non-conscious words, showing that conscious access has a brain-wide impact.
span.quote: Indeed, seen stimuli had a global impact on late evoked activity virtually anywhere in the cortex: 68.8% of electrode sites, although selected for clinical purposes, were modulated by the presence of conscious words (as opposed to 24.4% of sites for non-conscious words).

span.label: Transcranial magnetic stimulation over parietal or prefrontal cortex, far from visual areas, can block conscious perception and even make a fixated stimulus subjectively disappear.
span.quote: In normal subjects, transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) over either parietal or prefrontal cortex can prevent conscious perception and even trigger a sudden subjective disappearance of visual stimulis during prolonged fixation (Kanai et al., 2008)

span.label: Patients with focal prefrontal lesions needed stronger stimuli to see a masked target, in proportion to how far the lesion extended into left anterior prefrontal cortex, while their subliminal performance stayed normal.
span.quote: We recently made similar observations in patients with focal prefrontal lesions (Del Cul et al., 2009): their masking threshold was significantly elevated, in tight correlation with the degree of expansion of the lesions into left anterior prefrontal cortex, while subliminal performance on "not-seen" trials did not differ from normal.

span.label: Early-stage multiple sclerosis patients, whose white-matter damage disrupts long-distance connectivity, required a longer target-mask delay before a stimulus became conscious.
span.quote: As predicted, MS patients showed abnormal conscious perception of masked stimuli: they needed a longer target-mask delay before conscious access occurred.

span.label: The GNW model predicts and its simulations reproduce a strict seriality of conscious access, so only one content can be consciously processed at a time.
span.quote: A strict seriality of conscious access and processing is therefore predicted and has been simulated (Dehaene and Changeux, 2005; Dehaene et al., 2003b; Zylberberg et al., 2010).

span.label: Subliminal no-go signals activate only a small set of specialised inhibitory processors, whereas conscious no-go signals additionally recruit anterior cingulate, inferior and middle frontal gyrus, dorsolateral prefrontal and inferior parietal cortex.
span.quote: Only conscious no-go signals triggered a broad and more anterior activation expanding into anterior cingulate, inferior and middle frontal gyrus, dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and inferior parietal cortex – a network fully compatible with the GNW model (see figure 1).

span.label: Schizophrenic patients show impaired neural signatures of conscious access while their subliminal processing remains normal.
span.quote: Indeed, there is direct evidence for impaired neural signatures of conscious access, together with normal subliminal processing, in schizophrenic patients (Dehaene et al., 2003a; Del Cul et al., 2006; Luck et al., 2006).

span.label: The review's inventory of empirical markers of conscious access is: all-or-none prefronto-parietal ignition, all-or-none amplification of sensory activation, a late global P3b, late broad-band gamma power increase, enhanced long-distance beta-band phase synchronisation, and enhanced causal coupling between distant areas including a top-down component.
span.quote: In the present state of investigations, experimental measures of conscious access identified in this review include: (1) sudden, all-or-none ignition of prefronto-parietal networks; (2) concomitant all-or-none amplification of sensory activation; (3) a late global P3b wave in eventrelated potentials; (4) late amplification of broad-band power in the gamma range; (5) enhanced long-distance phase synchronization, particularly in the beta range; (6) enhanced causal relations between distant areas, including a significant top-down component.

span.label: conscious access
span.quote: In this review, we outline recent advances made in understanding the delimited issue of conscious access: how does an external or internal piece of information gain access to conscious processing, defined as a reportable subjective experience?

span.label: subliminal stimulus
span.quote: A subliminal stimulus is one in which the bottom-up, stimulus-driven information is so reduced as to make it undetectable, even with focussed attention.

span.label: preconscious stimulus
span.quote: A preconscious stimulus, by contrast, is one which is potentially visible (its energy and duration is such that it could be seen), but which, on a given trial, is not consciously perceived due to temporary distraction or inattention.

span.label: masking
span.quote: Subliminal presentation is often achieved by masking, a method whereby the subjective visibility of a stimulus is reduced or eliminated by the presentation, in close spatial and temporal contiguity, of other stimuli acting as “masks”(Breitmeyer, 2006).

span.label: subliminal priming
span.quote: Masked stimuli are frequently used to induce subliminal priming, the facilitation of the processing of a visible target by the prior presentation of an identical or related subliminal prime (for review, see Kouider and Dehaene, 2007).

span.label: attentional blink
span.quote: The attentional blink (AB) is a short-term variant of this effect where a brief distraction by a first stimulus T1 prevents the conscious perception of a second stimulus T2 briefly presented within a few hundreds of milliseconds of T1 (Raymond et al., 1992).

span.label: selection / selective attention
span.quote: Selection, also called selective attention, refers to the separation of relevant versus irrelevant information, isolation of an object or spatial location, based on its saliency or relevance to current goals, and amplification of its sensory attributes.

span.label: Global Neuronal Workspace
span.quote: Our proposal is that a subset of cortical pyramidal cells with long-range excitatory axons, particularly dense in prefrontal, cingulate, and parietal regions, together with the relevant thalamocortical loops, form a horizontal “neuronal workspace” interconnecting the multiple specialized, automatic and non-conscious processors (figure 6).

span.label: ignition
span.quote: Such a selfconnected system exhibits a dynamical threshold: if the incoming activity carries sufficient weight, it leads to the ignition of a self-supporting, reverberating, temporary, metastable, and distributed cell assembly that represents the current conscious contents and broadcasts it to virtually all distant sites.

span.label: Φ (integrated information)
span.quote: A notable feature of the dynamic core hypothesis is the proposal of a quantitative mathematical measure of information integration called Φ, high values of which are achieved only through a hierarchical recurrent connectivity and would be necessary and sufficient to sustain conscious experience

span.label: mismatch negativity (MMN)
span.quote: mismatch negativities (MMN), i.e. electrophysiological responses that arise primarily from the temporal lobe in response to rare, deviant or otherwise unpredictable auditory stimuli

span.label: stimulus amplitude and duration in the GNW network simulations
span.term: stimulus amplitude and duration in the GNW network simulations
span.quote: For very brief or low-amplitude stimuli, a feedforward wave was seen in the initial thalamic and cortical stages of the simulation, but it died out without triggering the late global activation, because it was not able to gather sufficient selfsustaining reverberant activation (Dehaene and Changeux, 2005).

span.label: attention and response requirements, equated between conscious and non-conscious trials
span.term: attention and response requirements, equated between conscious and non-conscious trials
span.quote: The effect is not easily imputable to increased post-perceptual processing or other task confounds, as many studies equated attention and response requirements on conscious and non-conscious trials

span.label: 68.8% / 24.4% — share of intracranial electrode sites whose late activity was modulated by conscious words versus by non-conscious words
span.quote: Indeed, seen stimuli had a global impact on late evoked activity virtually anywhere in the cortex: 68.8% of electrode sites, although selected for clinical purposes, were modulated by the presence of conscious words (as opposed to 24.4% of sites for non-conscious words).

span.label: 20% / 40% / 90% — proportion of recorded neurons whose firing followed the consciously perceived image during binocular rivalry, in V1-V2, in V4/MT/MST, and in IT/STS respectively
span.quote: The proportion of such cells increased from about 20% in V1/V2 to 40% in V4, MT or MST, to as high as 90% in IT and STS.

span.label: r²=0.96 — agreement across subjects between conscious perception thresholds estimated from objective performance and from subjective report in visual masking
span.quote: For instance, in visual masking, the conscious perception thresholds derived from objective and subjective data are essentially identical across subjects (r²=0.96, slope≈1) (Del Cul et al., 2006).

span.label: 86% sensitivity and 97% specificity — accuracy of predicting non-recovery one year after traumatic coma from diffusion tensor and spectroscopic measures of white-matter integrity
span.quote: In relation with the GNW model, it is noteworthy that prediction of non-recovery after 1 year could be calculated with up to 86% sensitivity and 97% specificity when taking into account both diffusion tensor and spectroscopic measures of cortical white matter integrity (Tshibanda et al., 2009).

span.label: 16 times — how many more dendritic spines layer-III pyramidal neurons carry in prefrontal cortex than in V1, cited as morphological support for long-distance integration
span.quote: Layer PFC pyramidal neurons have as many as 16 times more spines in PFC than in V1

span.label: ~50% — the level to which global cerebral metabolic activity typically falls in coma and vegetative state relative to normal
span.quote: In coma and vegetative state, as with general anesthesia, global metabolic activity typically decreases to ~50% of normal levels (Laureys, 2005).

span.label: 500 ms — elapsed time after which subliminal priming typically ceases to be detectable
span.quote: Second, subliminal priming decreases with elapsed time, and therefore typically ceases to be detectable after 500 ms (Dupoux et al., 2008; Greenwald et al., 1996; Mattler, 2005).

span.label: ~300-500 ms — latency of the P3/P3b component identified as the most consistent ERP correlate of stimulus visibility
span.quote: In ERPs, the most consistent correlate of visibility appears to be a late (~300-500 ms) and broadly distributed positive component called P3 or sometimes P3b

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1016/j.neuron.2011.03.018.
